question: What existing source-grounded evidence and reproducible methods constrain proposed glyph -> phonetic value -> acoustic/musical operation relationships across Paleo-Hebrew, Aramaic and English, without presupposing the recovered system?
case: Existing Aleph/A question reused, not a new all-letter reconstruction.
status: dated bounded scholarly baseline; instrument14/14 accounted; domain completeness OPEN

prior_art_reused.scope: Actual prior Jev1.14.0 Aleph/A selection and independent question wording
Reuse actual inspected sources/queries with their recorded limits

Reuse14-question instrument and P3 observation/decoding, P5 medium/context and P8 provenance/verification transfer limits; earlier different-domain subject matter does not establish ancient phonetics.

questions.question: Who has proposed this or something structurally equivalent before?
questions.answer: Davies edits inscribed Hebrew; Hanson and the Elephantine project edit Aramaic; Khan reconstructs a pronunciation tradition; CMUdict and Praat supply modern lexical/acoustic methods. Their component problems are prior art. No inspected source solves SUNNY's complete cross-tradition coupling.
questions.gap: A systematic historical census of explicit glyph-to-musical-operation proposals remains open.

questions.question: What fields study this problem?
questions.answer: Epigraphy, palaeography, historical phonology, textual criticism, grammatical morphology, pronunciation lexicography, acoustic phonetics and computational speech analysis address distinct links.
questions.gap: Ethnomusicology and source-native chant/ritual instruction need dedicated source work; sibling musical research remains separate.

questions.question: What terminology do those fields use for it?
questions.answer: ʾalef/aleph/ʾalaph, grapheme, sign token, transliteration, transcription, qere/ketiv, phoneme, allophone, orthoepy, non-consonantal, matres lectionis, phonation,F0,formant,spectral envelope,prosody and chant.
questions.gap: Terminological equivalence is not historical identity.

questions.question: What are the closest established theories, models, equations, or frameworks?
questions.answer: Edition-based reading constrained by manuscript/context; oral versus written transmission; one-to-many pronunciation lexicons; separate periodic-source and spectral-envelope measurements. Existing P0-A P3 distinction between latent state, observation and decoder transfers as method only.
questions.gap: Neither formal decoder vocabulary nor equal codepoint establishes a historical sound or musical operation.

questions.question: What reviews, surveys, bibliographies, encyclopedias, dissertations, or meta-analyses map the space?
questions.answer: Khan2020 and CAL bibliography workflows provide scoped routes; Davies and Hanson bibliographies identify primary editions. The earlier first-pass Cambridge Greek-alphabet summary remains a summary-only lead.
questions.gap: No systematic all-language review completed; current Neo-Aramaic/phonetics review coverage absent.

questions.question: What are the canonical papers, books, and authors?
questions.answer: Inspected work: Khan; Davies excerpt; museum TEI edited by VerenaLepper and collaborators; Hanson primary-text adaptation. Backward leads: Torczyner1938, Diringer1953, Sachau1911, Cowley1923, Porten/Yardeni1986.
questions.gap: The earlier cited editions were not all retrieved/collated, and canonical status across whole fields is not inferred from one bibliography.

questions.question: What are the competing explanations?
questions.answer: (A)Graphic inheritance with contextual phonetic reassignment; (B)bounded ritual/reading convention preserving specified pronunciation; (C)an operation acting on articulated gestures/phonological contrasts; (D)an operation on measured spectrum or relative pitch. Each requires different evidence and can coexist in separate contexts.
questions.gap: C/D are candidate formulations, not source-established ancient mechanisms. No arbitrary source weights select among them.

questions.question: What has been falsified, criticized, or abandoned?
questions.answer: The claim that every Alef in the inspected Tiberian tradition must be consonantal conflicts with Khan's explicit non-consonantal cases. A unique dictionary pronunciation for the English worda conflicts with two inspected entries. Treating every displayed Hebrew codepoint as the original ancient script confuses encoded transcription with artefact.
questions.gap: These are scoped counterexamples only; they neither refute a bounded ritual prescription nor SUNNY's adopted geometry.

questions.question: What are the unresolved questions?
questions.answer: Original intended symbol/sound coupling; the context-qualified ancient phonetic realizations; grammar and segmentation of selected target texts; operational units and native musical role; historical transmission bridges; applicable full-geometry realization and an independent distinguishing consequence.
questions.gap: No original ancient waveform or universal glyph-specific frequency identified in this inspected corpus.

questions.question: What primary sources or datasets are important to the field?
questions.answer: Lachish Letter2(edition1.002, museum1959,0711.2); Elephantine Pap.Cairo EM JdE43473/TAD A3.7; P13495/TAD A4.7 and its native date formula; Khan's cited Masoretic manuscripts/treatises; CMUdict; publisher's paired reconstructed readings; Praat methods.
questions.gap: Original inscription/papyrus facsimile collation, audio listening/measurement and full Latin witness remain unperformed.

questions.question: What earlier historical traditions have scholars already connected to it?
questions.answer: Unicode describes historic-script relationships; Khan links later reading reconstruction to particular medieval witnesses. Earlier project record retained Greek alphabet descent as a summary-only lead.
questions.gap: A scholarly historical connection between ancestry of letter forms and specific shared musical operation is not yet established.

questions.question: Has terminology changed over time in ways that hide older versions?
questions.answer: Search Paleo/Palaeo/OldHebrew, Phoenician/WestSemitic, Early/Imperial/OfficialAramaic, ʾalef/aleph/alaph, qere/ketiv, pronunciation/recitation/orthoepy, pitch versus formant. Modern normalized Hebrew display can hide a source's original script.
questions.gap: Aliases expand search coverage; they do not collapse traditions or times.

questions.question: Have adjacent disciplines rediscovered the same structure under another name?
questions.answer: A conditional mapping from visible sequence to possible latent readings resembles a decoder/inverse problem; dictionaries and acoustic estimation offer explicit alternatives and measurements. Reuse the formal distinction from archived P3/P5/P8.
questions.gap: This is a methodological analogy; independent historical rediscovery of SUNNY's full structure has not been shown.

questions.question: What obvious prior-art searches have produced nothing?
questions.answer: Targeted official-domain queries found no single direct BM page accessible through web tool(403), and no immediate exact-datedA3.7 entry. Those are access/query limits, not negative evidence. XML fallback successfully recoveredA3.7; direct official Aramaic date query led toP13495.
questions.gap: No adequate bounded negative search of ancient glyph-specific acoustic prescriptions completed; no novelty or absence claim follows.
